rows.quote: This analysis utilized publicly available datasets, including the BC Association Consortium (BCAC) 17, the UK Biobanking Study 21, the Finnish Genetics Study 22, and other large-scale GWAS (Table S1).
rows.reference_quote: Michailidou K, Lindström S, Dennis J. et al. Association analysis identifies 65 new breast cancer risk loci. Nature. 2017;551:92–4. doi: 10.1038/nature24284.
rows.coder_note: Step 2 (rules C5, F): the sentence attributes the BCAC dataset to reference 17, placed directly after the name (each dataset of the list carries its own number, so the mapping is explicit); its DOI 10.1038/nature24284 is the source of exactly one dictionary row (Michailidou 2017). The 122,977 cases and 105,974 controls of European ancestry given in p003 equal that row's; nothing conflicts. No accession.

rows.quote: Furthermore, summary-level data on genetic associations with BC were obtained from the FinnGen study's publicly available R10 dataset, which included 18,786 patients with BC and 182,927 controls.
rows.coder_note: Step 2 (rule A): the sentence gives the release identifier, 'the FinnGen study's publicly available R10 dataset'; the case and control counts are phenotype-specific and not a conflict (rule H). No accession.

Step 4 (rules D, I1): 'the UK Biobank database' with case and control counts only (9,721 / 351,473); counts with a cohort name alone do not identify a release. The reference attached to 'the UK Biobanking Study' (21, doi 10.1038/s41588-020-0621-6) is no dictionary row's source and cannot carry a code. The outcome side has UK Biobank rows, so rule C2 does not apply. No accession.
